scope: Recover a real PROTEI technical fingerprint without using Cuba as an anchor, validate it against confirmed non-Cuban deployments, and only then search for the same fingerprint elsewhere using passive/public evidence.
epistemic_firewall: A PROTEI vendor-family fingerprint is not automatically a PROTEI DPI-specific fingerprint.
A vendor deployment announcement is not by itself a remotely observable device fingerprint.
A country-level infrastructure-search hit is not sufficient to identify an operator or live host.
No live host/IP enumeration, credentials, exploit paths, or active scanning results are retained in this artifact.
Cuba is explicitly excluded as the evidentiary anchor for this pass.

confirmed_non_cuba_deployment_anchors.evidence: PROTEI states that deployment work was completed and its DPI platform was serving MegaCom commercial traffic.
The Fast Mode reported multiple PROTEI VAS and roaming solutions deployed at MegaCom and stated the relationship had continued since 2005.

confirmed_non_cuba_deployment_anchors.product_role: PROTEI DPI platform plus Policy Controller
confirmed_non_cuba_deployment_anchors.evidence: PROTEI states that the DPI platform was operating stably in the TT-Mobile network and serving real traffic.

independent_infrastructure_validation.finding: Citizen Lab reports that Censys and Shodan showed fingerprints of PROTEI equipment in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Russia when searched on 2022-11-30. The same report says RAEX IR.21 reporting data showed PROTEI as an equipment vendor in Jordan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan.
independent_infrastructure_validation.importance: This independently establishes that a PROTEI equipment fingerprint was observable in infrastructure-search data and that Kyrgyzstan had an independent telecom-equipment-vendor association with PROTEI.
independent_infrastructure_validation.limitation: Citizen Lab does not publish the exact Censys/Shodan query or raw host list in the report; this pass therefore does not claim to have reproduced those historical search-engine results.

evidence: A public Telegraf issue shows an operational PROTEI application returning this enterprise OID together with PROTEI-specific MIB names.
PROTEI documentation for multiple product families independently uses the same OwnEnterprise/sysObjectID value.

recovered_fingerprint_family.safety_note: Authentication secrets from vendor documentation are deliberately excluded.

fingerprint_validation_across_protei_pro.interpretation: The enterprise OID is a strong company/product-family fingerprint because it recurs across independent PROTEI product documentation and a real operational telemetry example. It is not unique to the DPI product line.

historical_independent_country_hits.source: Citizen Lab citing Censys/Shodan search on 2022-11-30

independent_equipment_vendor_association.source: Citizen Lab citing RAEX IR.21 reporting data

exact_public_string_search_this_pass.positive_matches: Vendor documentation and public software/telemetry discussions confirm the fingerprint itself, but do not safely bridge it to additional named operators in this pass.

next_collection_gates: Passively search public procurement, operator engineering documents, job postings, archived configuration excerpts, and support cases for the exact vendor-family markers.
Cross-match any recovered marker only against independently confirmed PROTEI customer/deployment records before promoting operator attribution.
For MegaCom and TT-Mobile, look specifically for a DPI-bound management/configuration marker rather than assuming that a generic PROTEI enterprise OID identifies the DPI node.
Search academic and measurement publications for packet-level behavior tied specifically to PROTEI DPI, keeping vendor-family and DPI-specific signatures separate.
Do not perform or retain live host enumeration, credential testing, or active exploitation.
